Thank you both for the thorough and constructive input. Let me summarize what I've heard before finalizing my decision.

From Marcus, I'm noting three key points: (1) Nora has an approved accommodation limiting her to exactly three concurrent client escalations and requiring written agendas and prompts at least two business days before performance-review discussions — and this case review qualifies as such a discussion, with proper notice confirmed for the record. (2) Nora's explanation that the handoff delays were tied to missing client inputs, not inaction, is a relevant factual observation for my assessment of whether a formal warning is warranted. (3) We need to verify whether Nora was actually assigned more than three concurrent escalations during the period in question — if so, that's an implementation gap on our side.

From Nora, I'm noting: (1) In each of the three missed handoffs, the required client inputs were missing when her work was due, she requested them in writing each time, and she completed the handoffs within one business day of receiving them. (2) She's already agreed informally to serve as a peer feedback partner for four weeks if I formalize that as a support measure. (3) She recommends a shared handoff checklist and respecting the workload accommodation as preventive measures.

From my own knowledge of the team context, I'm also noting that we handle several concurrent client escalations and that handoff expectations have not been written into a single shared checklist — which aligns with Nora's recommendation and suggests a systemic gap.

Before I finalize my decision, I want to address Marcus's third point: I need to verify Nora's actual workload assignments during the period in question against the three-concurrent-escalation limit. If she was assigned more than three, that's an implementation failure on our end that directly bears on this situation. I'll be making my decision with all of these factors in mind — the client-input dependency, the accommodation compliance question, and the lack of a shared handoff checklist.
